headline: Linklaters advises ReNew on recommended US$7.02/share take-private by CPP Investments–Sinha consortium via UK scheme
sum: Linklaters led a cross-practice team advising ReNew Energy Global Plc and its special committee of independent directors on a recommended all-cash take-private offer by a consortium of Canada Pension Plan Investment Board and founder-CEO Sumant Sinha at US$7.02 per share (later increased from US$6.75), valuing the UK-listed Nasdaq-traded company at approximately US$2.8 billion on a fully diluted basis. The transaction, announced as binding on August 11, 2026, is structured as a UK scheme of arrangement with rollover optionality and is subject to SEC/Nasdaq going-private rules, English corporate law, and Indian tax and restructuring regulations.
implication: Complex cross-border take-private of a UK-listed company with India-based operations exemplifies multi-jurisdictional M&A gating: UK scheme mechanics interact with US securities law (going-private notification, Form 6-K disclosure), Indian tax law, and post-closing reorganization into the private Indian subsidiary, requiring coordinated counsel teams across three jurisdictions.
detail: The consortium holds approximately 74% voting power (including JERA Nex's ~11.6% and Platinum Cactus's stake via ADIA). Non-consortium shareholders have the option to receive US$7.02 in cash or elect a rollover into the company's Indian subsidiary, with cash as the default. ReNew also agreed to sell 1,055 MW of solar assets in Rajasthan and Karnataka to Purvah Green Power for approximately US$537 million (INR 50.8 bn enterprise value), generating estimated INR 18.1 billion of cash inflows to support the financing. The transaction remains subject to UK court approval of the scheme and regulatory clearances in India.

framework.note: Statutory scheme of arrangement framework governs implementation mechanism, shareholder meetings, court sanctioning, and transfer of shares.

framework.note: Going-private transaction rules require specific SEC filings (Form 6-K), fair-dealing opinions, and disclosure of all material terms; gating document for US-listed foreign issuer.
Delisting rules, going-private transaction procedures, minority shareholder protections (independent committee, fairness opinions), and timing requirements for US exchange-listed company.

Taxation of share purchase consideration, reorganization of UK-listed structure into Indian private subsidiary post-closing, dividend distribution tax, and transfer pricing on intercompany transactions.
Outbound remittance of sale consideration by foreign shareholders, inbound investment by CPP Investments (foreign PE), repatriation of funds, and regulatory approvals from RBI.
Merger control clearance requirement if transaction meets threshold; filing with Competition Commission of India (CCI) likely required given combined enterprise value and turnover.
Power generation asset transfers (1,055 MW solar sale to Purvah Green Power) may require regulatory approvals from state electricity commissions and CERC for long-term PPA assignments.

framework.ref: Foreign Investment in India Policy 2020 & FIPB Rules
framework.note: CPP Investments (Canadian PE) inbound investment approval, sectoral caps in renewable energy, and DPIIT/FIPB clearances if applicable.
Post-closing restructuring of UK-listed ReNew Energy Global Plc into Indian private subsidiary (ReNew Private Limited); related-party transaction rules and minority shareholder protections.

approvals: UK High Court sanctioning of scheme of arrangement
ReNew shareholder meeting (for scheme and related arrangements)
Competition Commission of India (CCI) merger control clearance

structure.novel: Complex multi-jurisdictional mechanics: UK-listed company with India-based operations and Nasdaq trading; post-closing reorganization into private Indian subsidiary with rollover shareholders becoming direct shareholders of Indian entity; concurrent solar asset divestiture (1,055 MW) to generate liquidity; integration of going-private rules (SEC Rule 13e-3), UK scheme practice, and Indian tax/regulatory framework in a single binding transaction agreement.

triggers.note: Triggers mandatory going-private transaction notification, fairness opinion, and enhanced disclosure to SEC; filing of Schedule 13D amendments and Form 6-K.
Enterprise value (~US$10.2 bn) and turnover thresholds likely trigger CCI merger control notification requirement; filing may gate deal closure.
Cross-border fund flows (sale proceeds from non-consortium shareholders remitted to Canada; CPP capital injection) require RBI approval and LRS/ECB compliance.
1,055 MW asset sale to Purvah Green Power triggers PPA assignment approvals from CERC (central) and state regulators; impacts deal timing and structure.
Share transfer by non-consortium shareholders may trigger capital gains tax; reorganization into Indian subsidiary may be eligible for tax-neutral treatment if conditions met.
